message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I was in the right or wrong for locking my roommate and her friend out of our dorm room. Let me start by understanding the situation better. We live in a dorm room with two beds and two desks. My roommate and her friend have started doing something that's really annoying. Whenever my boyfriend and I are in our room, and they leave, they leave the door wide open. They laugh and say "this is what you get" as if it's for showing minimal PDA with my boyfriend in my room. But my boyfriend and I aren't doing anything; we're usually just watching Netflix in my bed. I feel like this is an invasion of my privacy. People in the dorm walk the halls, and I'm uncomfortable with that, especially since they're doing it intentionally to make me feel that way. Tonight, they left the room giggling and said "good luck" as they left the door open. They do this going in and out of the room like five times an hour. Each time I get up and close the door... I get sick of it on their like sixth trip, so I just lock the door. I know she has the key, but if I have to go through the hassle of getting up to close the door, they can go through the hassle of unlocking it. Anyway, the friend comes for their seventh trip and can't open the door and starts banging like crazy. I don't open the door because she knew what she was doing. She went back wherever she and my roommate were hanging and got the key and came in. Then she told me it was very rude that I locked the door because "it's my roommate's room." I calmly said if you're going to make me get up and close the door, you can go through the process of unlocking it. My boyfriend also asked why they were acting so passive-aggressive for no reason. She laughed and called me disrespectful again and left, leaving the door wide open. Am I really the asshole for just wanting my door kept closed so everyone passing by doesn't see me in my bed? Alright, so I need to figure out if I was right or wrong in this situation. Let's break it down. First, the issue is about privacy and the shared living space. My roommate and her friend are intentionally leaving the door open, which makes me uncomfortable. They seem to be doing this to assert some kind of control or to make me feel uneasy. On the other hand, I feel like I have the right to privacy in my own room, especially when my boyfriend is there. When I locked the door, I was trying to maintain my privacy and prevent them from barging in without knocking or respecting the closed door. However, by locking the door, I also prevented them from entering, which they saw as rude because it's technically their room too. I wonder if there's a middle ground here. Maybe instead of locking the door, I could have communicated my feelings more clearly or set some boundaries about the door being closed when we're in the room. Locking the door escalated the situation, leading to more conflict. But at the same time, I feel like my privacy is important, and I shouldn't have to compromise that just because they're being annoying. It's a shared space, but that doesn't mean I have to sacrifice my comfort and privacy. I also think about the concept of shared responsibility in a dorm. Both roommates should respect each other's space and find a way to coexist peacefully. Maybe talking to my roommate about this issue directly would help, rather than taking matters into my own hands by locking the door. In the end, I'm not sure if I was entirely right or wrong. I was trying to protect my privacy, but my method of locking the door might have been too harsh and led to more conflict. Perhaps there's a better way to handle this situation that respects both my need for privacy and their presence in the shared space.
